title: Internal Hom through the coefficient dual
statement:
Let $p,\ell$ be distinct primes, let $a,n\geq1$ be integers, put $q=p^a$, let $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ and $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, and let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be a finite extension with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$. Put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and choose $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$. Fix a six-functor datum [def-sf-datum] on separated finite-type $k$-schemes, with the coefficient categories, tensor and internal Hom of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and let $X$ be a scheme in this datum. Write $\Lambda_X$ for its coefficient unit (the constant finite coefficient sheaf at finite level and the completed coefficient sheaf at integral level, with rational and common-stage images at the field levels). Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ be quasi-isomorphic, locally on the coefficient site of $X$, to a bounded complex of finite projective $\Lambda_X$-modules: the local terms are direct summands of finite sums of the coefficient unit, with the localized and common-stage interpretations of [def-weil-site-perfect-complex]. Put $K^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_X(K,\Lambda_X)$. Then for every $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ the canonical evaluation comparison
$$
K^\vee\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}M\longrightarrow R\mathcal Hom_X(K,M)
$$
is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Write $K^\vee=R\mathcal Hom(K,\Lambda_X)$ and let $\theta_{K,M}:K^\vee\otimes^L M\to R\mathcal Hom(K,M)$ be the adjunct of evaluation, with the symmetry placing $K$ next to its dual. First work at finite coefficients. Choose a covering on which $K$ has a bounded finite-projective representative $P$, with $P^r=0$ outside $[a,b]$. By the definition of each finite-projective term, choose its finite free retraction; only finitely many nonzero terms require choices. These are degreewise splittings, not chain splittings. Restriction is exact, derived internal Hom commutes with slice restriction, and derived tensor commutes with the corresponding ringed-topos pullback. Thus the restriction of $\theta$ is the same evaluation comparison on the localized site. It suffices to calculate there; retain $R=\Lambda_X|_U$ for its ring sheaf.

For each term $E=P^r$, choose $E\xrightarrow{i}R^{\oplus m}\xrightarrow{p}E$ with $pi=1$. Its dual is a retract of $(R^{\oplus m})^\vee=R^{\oplus m}$ by dualizing $i,p$. Consequently both $E$ and $E^\vee$ are flat: tensor with either is a direct summand of the exact finite-sum functor $B\mapsto B^{\oplus m}$. Likewise $\mathcal Hom_R(E,-)$ is a direct summand of $\mathcal Hom_R(R^{\oplus m},-)=(-)^{\oplus m}$ and is exact. The ordinary evaluation isomorphism $B\otimes E^\vee\to\mathcal Hom_R(E,B)$ is precisely the one of the cited finite-projective evaluation lemma, which permits arbitrary module sheaves $B$. All these conclusions use only the displayed retraction, so also apply when $m=0$.

source.place: Tag 08JJ (lemma-dual-perfect-complex), last paragraph: finite free case and direct summands

proof.text: Put $D=\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(P,R[0])$, so $D^i=\mathcal Hom_R(P^{-i},R)$ and $d_D^i=(-1)^{i+1}(-\circ d_P^{-i-1})$. Step 2 verifies the exact-term hypothesis of the bounded-Hom lemma. For any representative $F$ of $M|_U$, that lemma applied to $F\to I(F)$ shows that $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,F)$ represents $R\mathcal Hom(P,M|_U)$; applied to $R[0]\to I(R[0])$ it shows that $D$ represents $(K^\vee)|_U$. Neither $F$ nor $I(F)$ is required to have constructible terms. The complex $D$ is bounded in $[-b,-a]$ with flat terms by step 2, hence is K-flat by the cited bounded-above flat criterion. Choose a K-flat flat-term resolution $Q\to F$. The cone of $D\otimes Q\to D\otimes F$ is canonically isomorphic to $D\otimes\operatorname{Cone}(Q\to F)$, by the total differential formula (multiply the shifted summand of degree $i$ in $D$ by $(-1)^i$), and is acyclic by the definition of K-flatness of $D$. The K-flat descent theorem computes the ordinary derived tensor by $D\otimes Q$; hence $\operatorname{Tot}(D\otimes_R F)$ computes it as well.

In total degree $n$, both complexes involve only $a\leq r\leq b$: the source is $\bigoplus_{i+j=n}(P^{-i})^\vee\otimes_R F^j$, and the target is $\prod_r\mathcal Hom_R(P^r,F^{r+n})$. The product has only finitely many possibly nonzero factors. On the summand $D^i\otimes F^j$ define $e^n(\phi\otimes m)$ to have its sole nonzero component at $r=-i$, sending $x$ to $(-1)^{ij}\phi(x)m$. Each diagonal component is the ordinary evaluation isomorphism of step 2, composed with symmetry and multiplication by $(-1)^{ij}$. Taking their finite direct sum gives an isomorphism $e^n$; its inverse applies the inverse evaluation separately in each component and the same sign. No infinite-product/direct-sum interchange occurs.

source.place: Tag 08JJ (lemma-dual-perfect-complex), the two displayed total complexes and final evaluation map

proof.text: The maps $e^n$ form a chain map. For $\phi\in D^i$ and $m\in F^j$, the $d_F$ component of $e(d(\phi\otimes m))$ has coefficient $(-1)^i(-1)^{i(j+1)}=(-1)^{ij}$, as in $d_{\mathrm{Hom}}e$. The precomposition-by-$d_P$ component has coefficient $(-1)^{i+1+(i+1)j}=(-1)^{ij+i+j+1}$, which equals the coefficient $-(-1)^{i+j}(-1)^{ij}$ from the Hom differential. Thus $e$ is a chain isomorphism. To identify the map, use the tensor-Hom adjunction with evaluation $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,F)\otimes P\to F$. The transpose of $D\otimes F\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,F)$ moves $P^r$ past $F^j$ in $D^i\otimes F^j\otimes P^r$, producing $(-1)^{rj}$, and then evaluates $D^i\otimes P^r\to R[0]$. The evaluation is zero unless $r=-i$, when $(-1)^{rj}=(-1)^{ij}$. This is exactly the displayed formula for $e$, so its derived image is the specified $\theta_{K,M}|_U$. This also proves compatibility with restriction and with morphisms of $M$, because the formula uses only composition, evaluation, and the coefficient action.

source.place: Tag 08JJ (lemma-dual-perfect-complex), evaluation comparison; signed differential calculation supplied here

proof.text: This proves the finite-level comparison on every member of the chosen covering. Its cone restricts to an acyclic complex there, because restriction is exact. Each cohomology sheaf of the cone is therefore zero locally: every section restricts to zero on a covering and is zero by the separatedness axiom for a sheaf. All its cohomology sheaves vanish, so the cone is zero in the derived category and the global $\theta_{K,M}$ is an isomorphism. This argument uses a cover of the site and does not replace site-perfectness by stalkwise perfectness.

source.place: Tag 08JJ (lemma-dual-perfect-complex), locality of the evaluation comparison

proof.text: At the integral stage use the completed coefficient sheaf specified in the definitions. Every reduction $K_n$ is site-perfect: apply reduction to the local representative and its degreewise finite-free retractions. The same interval $[a,b]$ works on each chosen covering object; no bound independent of the covering is needed. By the coefficient-comparison lemma, reduction of the actual map $\theta_{K,M}$ is the finite-level map $\theta_{K_n,M_n}$, including the identification of the coefficient dual and evaluation. Each is an isomorphism by steps 1--6. Both endpoints lie in the stated integral category of the six-functor datum; hence so does a cone $C$ by the integral triangulated-subcategory theorem. Derived reduction is exact, so every reduction $C_n$ is zero. By derived completeness, $C$ occurs in its Roos triangle $C\to\prod_n C_n\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_n C_n\to C[1]$. Both products are zero; thus $C=0$ and the integral comparison is invertible. In particular this argument uses the completed tensor of the datum; it never identifies that tensor with an uncompleted tensor without proof.

source.place: Coefficient clauses of sk-def-sf-operations; integral reduction and completeness argument supplementing the local proof

proof.text: At the rational stage $K,M\in D^b_c(X,E)$ are objects of $D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$, and by the coefficient-operation definition the rational evaluation comparison is the image under the localization functor $Q$ of the integral comparison $\theta_{K,M}$ (operations act on objects as the integral ones and on morphisms by linear extension). Since $D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ is a full subcategory of $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ and both Hom groups are tensored with $E$, $D^b_c(X,E)$ is a full subcategory of the ambient scalar localization $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)[1/\varpi_E]$. For an object $U$, [lem-sf-rational-slice-completed-evaluation] makes $j_U^*K,j_U^*M$ derived complete and carries $\theta_{K,M}$, also after scalar localization, to $\theta_{j_U^*K,j_U^*M}$. All local work below is done in the ambient scalar localizations on slices, so no constructibility of slice internal Homs is needed.

Fix a member $U$ of the chosen covering and put $M_U=j_U^*M$, derived complete by step 8. Let $\mathcal S_{M_U}$ be the class of objects $L$ of the derived category of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}|_U$-modules on the slice for which $Q(\theta_{L,M_U})$ is invertible in its scalar localization. The exactness and closure statement [lem-sf-rational-thick-evaluation], applied on the slice, puts the unit and zero in $\mathcal S_{M_U}$ and makes it closed under isomorphisms and retracts in the scalar localization, finite sums, shifts, and extensions.

source.place: Unit sk-prop-sf-dualizable-biduality, finite-free/retract and bounded-complex argument

proof.text: By the rational clause of the site-perfect definition, $j_U^*K\cong P$ for a bounded complex $P$ of module sheaves in degrees $[a,b]$ whose terms $P^r[0]$ are direct summands, in the scalar-localized category on $U$, of finite sums of the unit. The isomorphism and the retractions are morphisms with Hom groups those of the derived category on the slice tensored with $E$, so they hold in the ambient scalar localization. Write $\sigma_{\geq r}P$ for the brutal truncation (zero below $r$, unchanged from degree $r$ on). The sequence $0\to\sigma_{\geq r+1}P\to\sigma_{\geq r}P\to P^r[-r]\to0$ is split in every degree, so the degreewise-split triangle lemma gives a distinguished triangle with these three objects; its image under $Q$ is distinguished [lem-weil-linear-scalar-localization-triangulated]. Start at $\sigma_{\geq b+1}P=0$. Each $P^r[-r]$ lies in $\mathcal S_{M_U}$ by the unit, sum, retract and shift clauses of step 9. Descending induction gives $P=\sigma_{\geq a}P\in\mathcal S_{M_U}$, hence $j_U^*K\in\mathcal S_{M_U}$: $Q(\theta_{j_U^*K,j_U^*M})$ is invertible. For $V\to U$ the same holds over $V$, since restriction along $V\to U$ is an exact functor carrying this comparison to the one over $V$ (step 8).

For global rational detection: the rational internal Hom of the coefficient-operation definition is an operation only on pairs whose integral internal Hom is constructible, so the rational assertion concerns $M$ with $R\mathcal Hom(K,\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X})$ and $R\mathcal Hom(K,M)$ in $D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$; the completed tensor then lies there by the same definition. The rational comparison is $Q(f)$ for the integral numerator $f=\theta_{K,M}$ (step 8). Take an integral cone $C$ of $f$; it lies in the integral category by [lem-weil-integral-constructible-triangulated]. Since $Q$ is exact, $Q(f)$ is invertible exactly when $Q(C)$ is zero.

source.place: Local bounded-complex proof; scalar-localized local-to-global detection

proof.text: The finite-type definition gives a finite affine open cover of $X$. On each affine, the pro-etale covering definition refines the local-model cover by finitely many affine opens $W$ of its members. Collect these into a finite family $\{W_j\to X\}$; it is a covering, since $X$ is separated, so each $W_j\times_XV$ is affine for an affine open $V$ and finitely many of them cover $V$. By step 10 and the slice comparison, the restriction of $\theta_{K,M}$ to $W_j$ becomes invertible in the ambient scalar localization over $W_j$. Exact slice restriction carries the cone triangle of $\theta_{K,M}$ to one for the restricted map, so $C|_{W_j}$ has zero image there. The finite-cover localization lemma gives $N\geq0$ with $\varpi_E^N\mathcal H^d(C)=0$ for every $d$. For the empty scheme this holds without a nonempty covering.

source.place: Local bounded-complex proof; scalar-localized local-to-global detection expanded here

proof.text: By the integral-category definition, the reductions of $C$ have one cohomological interval $[u,v]$. Exact countable products put both products in its Roos triangle in $[u,v]$ as well. The long exact cohomology sequence thus gives $H^d(C)=0$ outside $[u,v+1]$. Apply the bounded-cone torsion lemma with the exponent $N$ from the preceding step and this finite interval: a power of $\varpi_E$ kills $\operatorname{id}_C$. Its rational image, and hence the rational cone of $\theta$, is zero. This proves the global rational comparison is invertible.

source.place: Local bounded-complex proof; scalar-localized local-to-global detection expanded here

proof.text: For $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, the definition of site-perfectness gives $K$ as the common-stage image of a site-perfect object over some finite coefficient extension. The common-stage definition likewise represents $M$ over a finite extension. Choose their compositum $L$, a finite common coefficient field, and extend both representatives to $L$. Exact scalar extension preserves the unit, finite sums, retractions and the finite cone construction of the local perfect model. Hence the representative of $K$ at this common field is still site-perfect. The coefficient comparisons identify the scalar-extended dual, tensor and internal Hom, and preserve evaluation; therefore they identify the representative of $\theta$ with the rational comparison over $L$ proved invertible in steps 8--13. That inverse over $L$ represents an inverse in the common-stage category, since its two inverse equations remain equations after passing to the common-stage morphism classes. Together with steps 1--7 this proves the assertion at every allowed coefficient stage.

split_report.summary: Repaired the returned split by extracting the hidden non-elementary arguments of former steps 8 and 9 into four statement-only lemma nodes: slice compatibility of completed and rational operations, triangulated closure of the rational evaluation class, finite-cover power-torsion detection, and bounded-cone torsion via truncations. Replaced the two overlong steps by six shorter steps preserving the original finite-level, integral, rational, and common-stage route. Maintainer reader (2026-10-17): steps 8-12 and three of the new statements recast in the ambient scalar localizations of the derived categories on slices, so that the local rational argument needs no constructibility of slice internal Homs; stale tool uses of the former step 9 removed.
split_report.blueprint: Finite-level local calculation in steps 1–6, integral reduction in step 7, rational slice compatibility and bounded-complex induction in steps 8–10, finite-cover detection and bounded-cone torsion in steps 11–13, and common-field passage in step 14. The route and proposition statement are unchanged.

tool_uses.why: Ordinary evaluation for a sheaf retract of a finite free module, valid for arbitrary target module sheaves; supplies the termwise calculation in the unit, not a replacement route.
Finite-filtration theorem for Hom complexes with exact termwise Hom; justifies the unit's passage from a bounded local model to derived Hom.
Bounded-above flat complexes are K-flat on any ringed site; justifies the local dual tensor representative.
Canonical computation of derived tensor using K-flat flat-term representatives.
Exactness of slice restriction, used for local calculation and local cohomology-sheaf detection.
Derived internal Hom commutes with slice restriction and takes triangles to triangles.
Monoidality of derived pullback for ringed topoi, applied to slice restriction.
Identifies finite reductions and scalar extensions of the actual dual/evaluation map, retaining the completed tensor at integral coefficients.
Ensures the cone of the integral comparison is derived complete, so reduction detects its vanishing.
Exactness of the derived reduction functor, used on the integral comparison cone.
Existence of flat-term K-flat resolutions for arbitrary complexes on a ringed site.
Exact termwise countable products in the pro-etale module category justify that the Roos construction commutes with finite mapping cones.
Exact scalar extension preserves the rational finite-filtration argument and the common coefficient field.
Bounds the cohomology of a derived-complete representative from its uniformly bounded reductions.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q94-7436887f3 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all four new nodes, the unit and chapter, the master and main-20261015 blueprint text, Stacks 08JJ and every cited statement in full. Steps 1-7, 13 and 14 are correct: I recomputed the signs in steps 4-5 (both components give (-1)^{ij}), and the bound of step 13, H^d(C)=0 outside [u,v+1], follows from the integral-category amplitude, exact countable products and the long exact sequence. The item statement is unchanged and not weakened. Fault 1 (E1/C4): step 10 applied the closure clauses of lem-sf-rational-thick-evaluation, which hold only 'whenever the objects lie in their stated domains', to sigma_{>=r}P and P^r[-r] on slices. The rational RHom (def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom) is defined only for pairs whose integral internal Hom is constructible, and nothing shows this on non-quasi-compact weakly etale slices. A rational retract of a constructible object need not be integrally constructible (Y+T with T a varpi^c-torsion object). For the same reason, local-global-power-torsion assumed slice constructibility and slice-completed-evaluation asserted it with no precise meaning. Repair: steps 8-12 and these three new statements now work in the ambient scalar localizations D(slice, O^)[1/varpi], where the completed tensor and RHom are always defined and the localization is triangulated. D^b_c(X,E) embeds fully there, so global invertibility is unchanged. The thick lemma now takes M derived complete, which the unit clause and the adjunct need. Local-global takes any C, with zero image equivalent to varpi^{N_j} id = 0. The slice lemma now asserts derived completeness of the restrictions, which is true because j^* is exact and sectionwise. Step 12 now justifies the finite covering by separatedness of X, and step 11 states the domain presupposition. Fault 2 (brief section 3): all four new nodes lacked merged_into and lean_audit; both are added. Three stale tool uses from the former step 9 are removed. All four new statements are true and were tested on small cases: N=0, u=v, C=0, t=0/X empty, a point. They are statement-only, strictly smaller than the item and duplicate nothing: grep of power-torsion, thick and Roos/slice nodes; lem-sf-generating-class-determination supplies only the formal closure. I accept the 14 remaining tool uses. No SGA source is used. Corrected files are in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-six-functors/ (the item and the four new nodes).; 5 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
